mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A three-month consecutive rise in unemployment rate above 9.0% signals deteriorating labor market health, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 9.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:HOUST at 593.0 and RSAFS at 360156.0 as of 2015-12-15
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent industrial production decline (INDPRO < 95.0) and unemployment rise (UNRATE > 9.0%) signal supply shock recession, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO at 92.5354 and UNRATE at 9.5% as of 2015-12-15
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 and UNRATE > 9.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals accelerating price pressures, prompting monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment decline (PAYEMS) and unemployment rise (UNRATE) indicate labor market contraction, reducing consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:PAYEMS at 130470.0 and UNRATE at 9.5% as of 2015-12-15
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion characterized by high consumer spending (RSAFS > 350000) and strong housing starts (HOUST > 600) leads to overvaluation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:RSAFS at 360156.0 and HOUST at 593.0 as of 2015-12-15
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 350000 and HOUST > 600.
